rundown: Tribe beat Cougars 85-39 at Kaplan Arena in Williamsburg, VA. Tribe led 41-28 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 100%).
Leading the way — Cougars: Timayahs Bracey 9 pts, 3 ast; Zach Skogen 8 reb. Tribe: ZZ Clark 16 pts; Jesse McIntosh 3 ast; John Roland Jr. 9 reb.
Where Tribe won it: they shot 50% to 26%, shot 30% from three to 16% and won the boards 46-32.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 20, 10:57 AM ET. It had Cougars 49% and Tribe 51%, projecting Cougars 81 – Tribe 81.4 (162.4 total, Tribe by 0.3).

Final: Cougars 39 – Tribe 85. Right winner: it had Tribe at 51%.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: AVER pts scored, AVER pts allowed, AVER lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Cougars came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 81, they scored 39 (−42 points, 52% under); projected to allow 81.4, they allowed 85 (+3.6 points, 4% over).

Tribe came in with a league-average attack and a 5% leakier than average defense (3-2, 86 scored and 86 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 184 and 185 games of evidence. Projected to score 81.4, they scored 85 (+3.6 points, 4% over); projected to allow 81, they allowed 39 (−42 points, 52% under).

The bigger miss was Cougars' scoring (-42 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 124 against 162.4 projected (-38.4), about the 1st percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Tribe by 46 against Tribe by 0.3 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (AVER pts scored, AVER pts allowed, AVER lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.749 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +46.8 points. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 814 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.980 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Tribe attack ×1.040, defense ×0.986 (5 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 45.7 points), no bet.
